output_list.reason: The 'transfer' function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The initial check 'if (balanceOf[msg.sender] < _value) throw;' is bypassed when the balance of the sender is at the boundary between zero and the transfer amount. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability to mint tokens for an arbitrary user.

The 'transferFrom' function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The initial check 'if (balanceOf[_from] < _value) throw;' is bypassed when the balance of the sender is at the boundary between zero and the transfer amount. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability to mint tokens for an arbitrary user.

The 'mintToken' function has a wrong logic vulnerability. It directly assigns balance to target without checking if the target is a valid user. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability to mint tokens for an arbitrary user.

The 'buy' function has an integer overflow vulnerability. It calculates the amount of tokens to sell by dividing the amount of ether sent by the buy price. If ether sent is at the boundary between zero and the buy price, the buy price will be zero, allowing an attacker to buy an arbitrary amount of tokens.
